dates.altered: The entry records the house 'extended c.1670 probably for Thomas Turner; late C18 and C19 additions and alterations'.
dates.note: The entry says 'Circa 1570 for Richard Turner'; the Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built | 1570' without the circa, and a tourist-board page read the same day says 'built around 1600'. The list entry's own circa is what this record carries.

quotes.text: Shown on O.S. map as Manor House. Manor house. Circa 1570 for Richard Turner, extended c.1670 probably for Thomas Turner; late C18 and C19 additions and alterations; between 1871 and 1896 it was the home of William Morris.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: Uncoursed limestone rubble with alternating angle quoins; stone slate roofs with moulded coped verges, parapet and ball finials to gables.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, materials sentence following the opening paragraph

quotes.text: Original house a U-plan with main range of 3-unit through-passage type and gabled ranges projecting to rear; extended at right-angles to east on north in late C17. 2 storeys and attics.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, plan and storeys sentences following the materials sentence

quotes.text: East (entrance) front. 3 bays; mullion windows with dripstones, of 4 lights to ground floor, 3 lights to first floor except centre of 2 lights and of 2 lights to prominent gabled full dormers to left and right.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, description of the east front

quotes.text: Prominent external end stack to left has 2 detached diagonal shafts with moulded capping and rectangular windows to left; similar ridge stack to right with 3 detached shafts.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, east front continued; this span sits in the third block returned by the extract

quotes.text: West front: has projecting gables to left and right, left longer and flush gable to centre. All have 2-, 3- and 4-light mullion windows with dripstones to attic, first floor and ground floor respectively, except for right gable which has half-glazed stable door in earlier surround with rectangular chamfered window to right on ground floor.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, description of the west front

measurements.note: The main range. This is the same plan word the Grevel's House entry uses ('7 units') and the two are not on the same scale; a unit here is a room-width bay of a three-room through-passage house.

measurements.note: The east front. The same sentence gives 3 lights to the first floor and 2 to the dormers, so the diminishing course of lights up the elevation is stated twice in this cluster -- here and at Owlpen Manor -- by two different surveyors.

note: Tranche 3, the English cottage and the Cotswold vernacular, 5 Sep 2026. Added by this tranche. Kelmscott is on the eastern edge of the node's stated hearth ('west Oxfordshire') and is here for a reason the node's own prose supplies: it is the house William Morris took as the standard of unforced building, and the link from the district's masons to Arts and Crafts runs through it as much as through Sapperton. The entry is the cleanest statement in this cluster of the Cotswold elevation grammar -- uncoursed rubble, dressed quoins, coped verges with ball finials, and lights falling 4 - 3 - 2 from ground to attic.
